rv.q: Not even the strong singing of Nicola Hughes, who plays a disgruntled lover, or Sally Ann Triplett, as a wild-haired babysitter, can save this production from confusion and cliche.
Hitchcock-inspired musical suffers from an identity crisis
Lutvak’s music is in-yer-face and largely formulaic, including everything that a great musical theatre score should have, but it never quite convinces.
A couple of creative tweaks could undoubtedly see this be a killer success but, in its current form, it is sadly more of a misfire.
